paragraphs: Enevo sells waste container sensors and a cloud software platform to haulers, waste services companies, property managers, cities and campuses that want a clearer picture of their waste operations. The stated point of collecting that data is to let an operator control collection better and improve recycling rates.

Sensors report hourly fill levels and collection events, and the platform turns those readings into trends showing when a container needs picking up. An alert system flags sudden build ups and unforeseen events such as theft, fire or vandalism. A routing engine and scheduler compares service needs against available truck resources and proposes changes based on fill level trends and seasonal variation. Drivers work from an app built around routing, navigation and reporting. Historical fill and collection data can be pulled into other systems through a REST API.

The company says it was founded in 2010 by veterans of the wireless and telecom industry. Its customers run from small regional recyclers to large national waste management companies. Enevo also names property managers, cities, municipalities and higher education and corporate campuses among the groups whose waste data needs it serves.
